items.title: [FDD Diary #001] I Thought It Worked
content:
Fury-Driven Development.

Can't code. Not a developer.
Built a product with AI anyway.
Then the whole system died.

This is the diary of what happened.

FDD Diary #001 🧵

ChatGPT for two years.
Ask a question, get a code block.
Copy. Paste. Error.
Copy the error. Ask again.
Paste. Error.

Never escaped that loop.

Then I heard about Claude Code.
Installed it. Typed "make me a to-do app."

It didn't show me code.
It made the files directly.

Folders created. Code written. Packages installed.

Five minutes.
What took three hours with ChatGPT took five minutes.

"Notes app." Done.
"Database." Done.
"Login." Done.

Built a stock screener in two days.
586 US stocks, three strategies, done in 3 minutes.

"Run this every day." Done.
"Send to Slack." Done.

Three days in I had five agents running.

Am I a genius?
I knew I wasn't. But it felt that way.

"I can build anything with this."

That thought. That feeling.
That was the trap.

https://vibecode.town/posts/i-thought-it-worked

items.title: [FDD Diary #002] Monday Morning
content:
Monday morning.
Made coffee. Turned on the monitor.

The whole system was dead.

FDD Diary #002 🧵

I built it the same way I built the to-do app.

"Add file sync." Done.
"Add remote commands." Done.
"Add monitoring." Done.

Like assembling IKEA furniture.
I never stopped to ask if the pieces fit together.

Opened the code. Can't read it. But I can scroll.

10,847 lines.
Almost half was duplicated. 4,200 lines.

Five agents built the same function five different ways.
Three date formatters. Two config parsers.

Nobody noticed. Not the AI. Not me.

Ran a security audit. Line 847.
Shell injection.

This tool connects my computers over a network.
A shell injection means anyone can walk in and run anything.

That's not a bug. That's a door.
That door was open the whole time.

That night I shut everything down.
Stared at ten thousand lines.

"What the hell am I even building?"

https://vibecode.town/posts/everything-broke-monday

items.title: [FDD Diary #003] Nothing Works
content:
Three computers at home.
Two desktops, one laptop.

I want to work from my laptop outside
and still use the machines at home.

Nothing on the market does this.

FDD Diary #003 🧵

KVM switch — physical only. No network.
Remote Desktop — slow. Drops connection.
Cloud sync — files only. No processes.
Git — code only. Large files? No.

Five apps running at once just to get "barely okay."

Barely. Okay.

Every morning: open five apps, remember where everything is, manually fix sync conflicts.

That's not work. That's busywork.

So I decided to build it myself.

It wasn't "decided to build it" first.
It was "figured out why nothing works" first.

Every product I tried, I knew what pissed me off about it.

That list of grievances?
The beginning of a spec.

https://vibecode.town/posts/frustration-is-the-spec
